2. This is first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail relating to Crime No.555/2023, dated (not mentioned)
registered at Police Station-Raipuria, District-Jhabua (M.P) for the offence under Sections 420, 409,
34 of IPC and under Section 6 of Nikshepakon ke Hiton ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000.

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 24.09.2024.
3. As per prosecution story, it is alleged that the applicant has committed forgery with the complainant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.

The applicant is said to be Director of the company and he has obtained Rs.
8,64,000/- for making the amount double.

The said amount was taken in the year 2011 and the FD NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31992 2 MCRC-46963-2024 of has been matured in the year 2017 but the FIR is registered in the year 2023 which is delayed by six years.

The applicant is ready to deposit Rs. 3 Lakhs before the learned Trial Court and the respondent may be permitted Sanjay Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112161143/
1 to withdraw the amount subject to appropriate conditions.

sentences.text:
Earlier, two co- accused persons namely Kesuram and Ganpat have been released on bail after depositing of Rs. 5 Lakhs and 2 Lakhs,
respectively.
The case of present applicant is having complete parity with the co-accused persons.
The applicant is in custody since 24.09.2024.
Final conclusion of trial will take a sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.

6. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the allegations and custody period of the applicant, and mainly the fact that the applicant is ready to deposit Rs.3 Lakhs, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Consequently, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed under the following conditions:-
i. Subject to depositing before the Trial Court an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- by the applicant at the time of furnishing the bail bond and Trial Court shall open an FD of the aforesaid amount in a Nationalized Bank.

ii. Applicant shall furnish a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31992 3 MCRC-46963-2024 the satisfaction of the trial Court,
for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
iii. Complainant is permitted to withdraw the amount so deposited by the applicant subject to furnishing adequate security before the trial Court.

iv. The applicant shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
